articles.title: Cloud Engineering in Practice: How Teams Make Cloud Platforms Reliable, Secure, and Affordable
articles.excerpt: Most teams do not struggle with the cloud because they chose the wrong provider. They struggle because the platform grew one manual decision at a time: an environment configured by hand here, a pipeli…
articles.body: Most teams do not struggle with the cloud because they chose the wrong provider. They struggle because the platform grew one manual decision at a time: an environment configured by hand here, a pipeline exception there, a security review after go-live, and a cost report nobody owns. Cloud engineering is the discipline that turns that accumulation into a system. This article breaks down what that system looks like in practice — the layers, the controls, and the warning signs that a platform needs engineering attention rather than another quick fix. The warning signs A cloud platform usually needs structured engineering work when several of these show up together: Environments behave differently.

articles.title: Docker Bypasses UFW: Your Firewalled Database Is Probably Public. Here's the Fix
articles.excerpt: If you run ufw default deny incoming on a VPS and then docker run -p 5432:5432 postgres, your Postgres is reachable from the whole internet. UFW will still tell you everything is denied. Docker has by…
articles.body: If you run ufw default deny incoming on a VPS and then docker run -p 5432:5432 postgres , your Postgres is reachable from the whole internet. UFW will still tell you everything is denied. Docker has bypassed UFW since at least 2014, and the fix is a one-line change most people never hear about. This week's Docker is weird essay made the rounds on Hacker News and Lobsters . It's a fun tour of internals: containers are just processes, images are just folders, runc re-execs /proc/self/exe because Go can't fork. All of it is true and weird, and none of it will get your database dumped by a bot at 3am. The weird default that will is buried in the comments.

articles.body: Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation for deep-sea exploration habitat design for low-power autonomous deployments Introduction: A Lesson from a Drowning Sensor My learning journey into this topic began with a failure. While experimenting with a small autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) prototype in a shallow test tank, I watched a multi-modal perception stack — stereo cameras, a forward-scan sonar, and an acoustic Doppler current profiler — drain the battery in under four hours. The vehicle was supposed to map a simulated hydrothermal vent field autonomously. Instead, it went dark, and I spent the afternoon fishing it out of the water with a pool net, feeling equal parts embarrassed and curious.

articles.title: Computer Simulations for Students: Why Testing a Virtual World Can Teach Us About the Real One
articles.excerpt: Imagine a student trying to understand why traffic builds up at a busy intersection. A textbook can explain traffic signals, vehicle movement and road capacity. A diagram can illustrate how cars trave…
articles.body: Imagine a student trying to understand why traffic builds up at a busy intersection. A textbook can explain traffic signals, vehicle movement and road capacity. A diagram can illustrate how cars travel through an intersection. But what happens if the traffic signal stays red for longer? What if twice as many cars arrive? What if another lane is introduced? These questions are difficult to explore through a static diagram. With a computer simulation, students can change the conditions, observe what happens and compare different outcomes. This is what makes computer simulations for students an interesting part of modern education. They allow learners to investigate situations that may be difficult, expensive, time-consuming or impractical to recreate physically.

articles.title: Tired of rebuilding patched APKs? These Morphe community projects handle them for you
articles.excerpt: You can simplify patched Android app updates with self-hosted AutoMorph or cloud-based Mophe-AutoBuilds.
articles.body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Manually updating Morphe-patched Android apps requires regularly and repeatedly downloading base APKs, running Morphe Manager, and applying updates by hand, potentially across multiple devices. AutoMorph automates the entire workflow via a Docker container on a homelab server. It automatically scrapes APKs, compiles builds daily, and supports custom keystores for seamless updates. Mophe-AutoBuilds pairs GitHub Actions with Obtainium for hands-off background updates, though it requires trusting pre-compiled APKs signed with shared community keys. Community patching tools, namely Morphe , have made it remarkably easy to tweak and de-bloat popular Android apps .

articles.title: 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds
articles.excerpt: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of dark matter, the mysterious stuff that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.
articles.body: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds. For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter , whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe . Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

articles.body: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23). The mission lifted off aboard an Electron rocket from Rocket Lab’s New Zealand launch site today at 3:11 a.m. EDT (0711 GMT; 8:11 p.m. local time in New Zealand). The Electron carried three "Hawk" satellites for the Virginia-based company HawkEye 360, which explains the name Rocket Lab gave to the mission: "We're Not Hawking Around." If all goes according to plan, the three Hawks will be deployed into low Earth orbit (LEO), at an altitude of 323 miles (520 kilometers). Once up there and commissioned, the satellites will scan the globe for radio frequency (RF) emissions.

articles.title: Space debris: Are we on track for true sustainability? (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: Space is a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. It’s therefore critical to maintain a safe and clean orbital environment.
articles.body: David Zamora is the chairman of the Space Data Association. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The commercialization of space is well underway, and as a result, Earth’s orbit is becoming ever more congested. The current number of active satellites in orbit stands at around 16,000, according to the European Space Agency( ESA), and this number is expected to jump close to 60,000 by 2035, Novaspace projects . While it’s not always given the recognition it deserves, space has fast become a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. Therefore, it’s critical that a safe and clean operating landscape is maintained.

articles.title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
articles.excerpt: The full-scale prototype of Europe's Space Rider orbiter failed to deploy its parachute during a drop test earlier this month, but ESA officials hope the setback won't delay progress toward its first…
articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.title: Canva’s first AI image model plans designs before generating them
articles.excerpt: Canva is diving even deeper into AI with the launch of an image generation model that competes directly with those from OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. The model, called Canva Craft, uses a two-stage a…
articles.body: Canva is diving even deeper into AI with the launch of an image generation model that competes directly with those from OpenAI, Microsoft, and Google. The model, called Canva Craft , uses a two-stage architecture that allows it to plan a design before generating an image, allowing for "greater precision, consistency and control," according to an announcement on Thursday . Canva Craft can generate images at up to 2K resolution and in more than 30 aspect ratios. In addition to generating social media posts and marketing content, it's also supposed to create realistic scenes, digital art, environmental imagery, and more. articles.title: NASA Invites Media to 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium
articles.excerpt: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s sym…
articles.body: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s symposium is focused on humanity’s return to the Moon, sustainable lunar infrastructure, advanced space propulsion, and the evolving space workforce. Panels include discussions on Artemis II and III, space propulsion flash talks, building utilities and infrastructure for sustainable lunar operations, Moon base supply chain resilience, space nuclear technology, navigating the new NASA workforce, and engineering the future, featuring keynotes and awards presentations.
